title: Request Surface Replay & Synthetic Corpus Builder
author: Aisha Nguyen
content:
Summary
-------
This document describes the canonical process and tooling to produce replayable request surfaces and synthetic request corpora for benchmarking, profiling, and regression tests of the Redwood inference runtime. The corpus builder produces privacy-validated payloads, stratified sampling artifacts, and annotated replay manifests that drive the microbench, end-to-end, and kernel-level perf suites.

Goals
-----
- Provide reproducible, representative request sets that reflect production request shape (tokens, context windows, multimodal markers, KV cache patterns).
- Enable deterministic replay for latency, tail analysis, and kernel-sensitivity tests.
- Produce anonymized synthetic variants for open benchmarking and distributed perf teams.
- Integrate with existing perf harnesses and the profiling playbook to link input tokens to kernel execution traces.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
In scope:
- Extraction and normalization of request metadata from live sampling channels (telemetry/ingress-proxy).
- Sampling strategies that preserve per-tenant request distributions.
- Tools to synthesize requests that preserve statistical properties while removing PII.
- Output formats and manifests consumed by the benchmarking suite and runtime profilers.

Out of scope:
- Full conversational session reconstruction (this builder targets single-request / short-session replay).
- Long-term storage policy (see data-residency-and-retention policy).

When to use this builder
------------------------
- Before kernel rollouts to verify sensitivity across representative inputs.
- Prior to model-variant release to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.
- During incident postmortems where a reproducible input is needed for hypothesis testing.

High-level design
-----------------
1) Ingress sampling: live request sampler emits lightweight records to the sampling pipeline (ingest topic: perf-samples).
2) Normalizer: canonicalizes fields (prompt, metadata, token counts), computes derived features (prompt_length, kv_hits_est), and marks candidate PII spans.
3) Sampler & stratifier: chooses records by tenant, model, time-of-day, and sequence-length bucket; produces a replay_manifest.json.
4) Anonymizer & synthesizer: replaces PII using deterministic synthetic replacement; can optionally generate paraphrases and temperature variations.
5) Exporter: writes artifacts to artifacts/perf-corpora/<corpus-name>/ with a defined structure for the benchmark harness.

Data model and manifest format
----------------------------
The pipeline emits two artifact types: raw_sample_records (for internal debugging) and replayable_corpora (used by benchmarks). A sample replay manifest (replay_manifest.json) has these top-level fields (text form):

- name: string (corpus ID)
- created_at: ISO timestamp
- sample_count: integer
- stratification: list of {dimension:bucket-definition}
- files: list of {path:relative/path.jsonl, compression:gzip|none, record_schema: v1}
- privacy_level: none|anonymized|synthetic
- producer_version: semver

Record schema (line-delimited JSON): each line is a request record with flattened fields to simplify ingestion. Example (single line):
{\n  \"request_id\": \"r-01234\", \"tenant\": \"t-company-x\", \"model\": \"redwood-7b-v1\", \"prompt\": \"Summarize the quarterly KPIs...\", \"prompt_tokens\": 124, \"max_tokens\": 256, \"response_expected\": true, \"kv_cache_hint\": 0.2, \"metadata\": {\"route\": \"/generate\", \"region\": \"us-west-2\"}\n}

Note: the manifest and record schema are stored as flat JSONL; nested maps in \"metadata\" must be stringified to keep ingestion tooling simple.

Sampling and anonymization guidance
----------------------------------
- Minimum sample sizes: for per-tenant test corpora aim for 10k requests or 1% of tenant traffic, whichever is smaller.
- Buckets: use token-length buckets {0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048, 2049+} and priority buckets (real-time, background, batch).
- Differential privacy step: for public synthetic exports, apply a DP noise layer to counts (epsilon configurable; default 1.0) before publishing aggregate summaries.

Anonymization modes:
1) anonymized: redact or replace email/phone/account ids with deterministic tokens (user_00001).
2) synthetic: generate paraphrases that preserve language features (POS distribution, length) but not original content; used for customer-sharable corpora.

Anonymization table (example)
Field | Action | Notes
------|--------|------
email | replace | deterministic hash -> user_{n}
phone | redact | replace with \"<PHONE>\"
account_id | token -> ACC_{n} | preserve stable id mapping for replay correlation
free_text_prompts | PII detect + paraphrase | optional paraphrase to preserve token shape

Pipeline: step-by-step runbook
-----------------------------
Prerequisites:
- Access to sampling topic (infra role: perf-sampler-reader).
- S3 write access to artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/<team>/

1) Create a new corpus definition:
   - File: pipelines/corpus-defs/<corpus-name>.yaml
   - Required fields: name, target_window (UTC), privacy_mode, stratification_rules, sample_goal

2) Dry-run extract (no PII transformation):
   $ tools/corpus-builder extract --config pipelines/corpus-defs/<corpus-name>.yaml --mode dry-run --out /tmp/corpus-dryrun
   - Verify sample_count and bucket distribution in /tmp/corpus-dryrun/preview.json

3) Commit anonymization policy and run full build:
   $ tools/corpus-builder build --config pipelines/corpus-defs/<corpus-name>.yaml --out s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/benchmarks/<corpus-name>/ --anonymize

4) Validate artifacts with harness smoke test (local runner):
   $ perf-harness run --corpus s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/benchmarks/<corpus-name>/replay_manifest.json --verify-schema

5) Schedule the corpus for perf runs (Jenkins or prow job): add to nightly-bench.yaml with job label corpora/<corpus-name>.

CLI examples and tips
---------------------
- To generate a small dev corpus (100 records) focused on long prompts:
  $ tools/corpus-builder extract --config pipelines/corpus-defs/long-prompts.yaml --sample-goal 100 --filter \"prompt_tokens>512\" --out ./dev-corpora/long-100

- To create a synthetic public corpus with paraphrases and DP on aggregates:
  $ tools/corpus-builder build --config corpora/public-synthetics.yaml --privacy synthetic --dp-epsilon 0.8 --out s3://redwood-public-benchmarks/synthetics/v1

Storage layout and artifact naming
--------------------------------
Artifacts must follow this layout in the artifacts bucket: 

s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/benchmarks/<corpus-name>/
  - replay_manifest.json
  - records.v1.jsonl.gz
  - integrity.sha256
  - summary.statistics.json
  - annotations/kernel-hints.csv
  - provenance/build-metadata.json

Naming conventions: use lowercase, dashes, and a date suffix for iterative builds (e.g., retail-2025-11-03).

Integration points with profiling and benchmarking suites
---------------------------------------------------------
- perf-harness consumes replay_manifest.json and maps each record to a bench case. The harness will optionally attach kernel hint annotations to tracer spans using annotations/kernel-hints.csv.
- runtime-tracer expects the corpus to include \"kv_cache_hint\" and \"prompt_tokens\" fields to optimize tracing bucketization.
- Use the \"profiling:enrich\" step to precompute per-record kernel selection expectations (tools/corpus-builder enrich --out annotations/).

Metrics and SLOs we track for corpora-driven runs
------------------------------------------------
- baseline_throughput_rps: expected throughput for the mixed workload (target is corpus-specific).
- p50, p95, p99 generation_latency_ms: compare to declared baseline; regression threshold = +20% p95 or +50% p99.
- kernel_error_rate: percentage of runs that triggered fallback kernels; regression threshold = 2% absolute increase.
- trace_coverage: fraction of records that produced full kernel traces (target >= 90%).

Ownership and responsibilities
------------------------------
- Producer: perf-platform team (owner: Ravi Singh) — defines sampling windows and maintains extractors.
- Maintainer: serving-runtime/benchmarking (owner: Aisha Nguyen) — maintains corpus-builder tooling and manifests.
- Privacy reviewer: security-and-compliance (owner: Lena Hofstad) — approves synthetic/public exports.

Rollout checklist for a new corpus
----------------------------------
- [ ] corpus definition YAML checked into pipelines/corpus-defs/
- [ ] dry-run sample preview reviewed (buckets, tenant balance)
- [ ] anonymization policy approved by privacy reviewer
- [ ] artifacts built and verified by perf-harness smoke test
- [ ] job added to nightly-bench and merged
- [ ] metrics alerts configured for regression thresholds

Troubleshooting common failures
-------------------------------
- Missing records in manifest: confirm the sampler had permissions; check perf-samples topic lag.
- Schema verification fails: run tools/corpus-builder lint --schema v1 and inspect errors.
- Low trace_coverage: ensure profiler sidecar is enabled for the target bench job and tags (kernel-hints) are present in annotations.

Appendix: example corpus-def YAML
--------------------------------
name: dev-long-prompts-2025-03
target_window: 2025-03-01T00:00:00Z/2025-03-01T06:00:00Z
privacy_mode: anonymized
stratification_rules:
  - dimension: prompt_tokens
    buckets: [\"0-32\", \"33-128\", \"129-512\", \"513-2048\"]
sample_goal: 10000
filters:
  - expression: \"model==\\\"redwood-7b-v1\\\" and region==\\\"us-west-2\\\"\"
